body:
```suggestion
			If [code]true[/code], attempts to disable the threaded optimization feature in NVIDIA drivers, which is known to cause stuttering in most OpenGL applications.
			This is done by enabling minimal OpenGL debug logging and ignoring its output, which can force the driver to disable threaded optimization.
			[b]Note:[/b] This setting only works on Windows, as threaded optimization is disabled by default on other platforms.
```

"_Only works on Windows_" is true judging by this PR, but it's a bit of a weird contradiction, because "_disabled by default on other platforms_" implies it **can** be enabled on said platforms, if somehow desired, which makes the setting relevant on all platforms.
That's to say I am not sure "by default" is the correct term here.

body:
It is disabled by default on Linux, but afaik can be enabled by setting environmental variable:
```
__GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS=1
```
Linux afaik also has an automated self-disabling mechanism to try and detect if the optimization is hurting performance.

The problem is that we have no confirmation that debug logging also fixes the problem on other platforms. But given that it requires a specific step to _turn it on_ in the first place on Linux, I'm inclined to leave this until it is reported as a real issue in the wild, because turning on debug logging could possibly degrade performance when threaded optimization is already off (this is also an issue for windows, and why I'm kind of unsure about whether we should be using this method _at all_).

But yes, this could be better worded, maybe something like:
> This setting takes effect only on Windows, where the problem is confirmed to occur, and debug logging is confirmed to fix it.
> On Linux, NVIDIA threaded optimization is currently disabled by default by the graphics driver (although can be enabled).
